what_its_for: Adalimumab-aqvh is used to reduce inflammation and treat several conditions including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis (spine inflammation), Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis in children. It works by blocking a protein in your body called TNF-alpha that causes inflammation and damage to your joints, skin, and digestive tract.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your thigh or belly area (at least 2 inches away from your belly button). It comes as a prefilled syringe or autoinjector pen. Rotate your injection sites each time so you do not inject in the same spot twice in a row. Never inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, hard, or scarred. Allow the pen or syringe to sit at room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes before injecting — do not warm it in a microwave or hot water. Clean the injection site with an alcohol wipe and let it dry before injecting. A caregiver or nurse can help teach you how to inject this medicine properly.
dosing: Your dose and how often you inject will depend on the condition being treated. Common dosing examples include: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, or ankylosing spondylitis — 40 mg every other week. Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis — a higher starting dose is given for the first few injections, then 40 mg every other week. Plaque psoriasis — 80 mg as a starting dose, then 40 mg every other week starting one week after the first dose. Your doctor will tell you the exact dose and schedule that is right for you. Always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then continue your regular schedule from that point forward. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your normal schedule. Do not inject two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store adalimumab-aqvh in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 14 days in the original carton — write down the date you took it out of the refrigerator and throw it away after 14 days even if there is medicine left. Do not shake the pen or syringe. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used needles and syringes in a proper sharps container — do not throw them in the regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as live flu vaccine, MMR, or chickenpox vaccine) while using this medicine — talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, especially those with infections such as tuberculosis (TB), chickenpox, or shingles, because this medicine weakens your immune system and makes it harder for your body to fight infections. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it may worsen some side effects. Tell your doctor if you are planning to have surgery or a dental procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, cough that won't go away, shortness of breath, burning when urinating, or unusual wounds that won't heal; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; chest pain or a new or worsening cough; numbness or tingling in your hands or feet; vision changes; new or worsening weakness; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain; new skin lumps or open sores; or any signs of unusual bleeding or bruising. Also tell your doctor if you have been exposed to tuberculosis or hepatitis B.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement within 2 to 4 weeks of starting treatment, but it can take 3 to 6 months to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Do not stop using it just because you feel better — this medicine works best when used on a long-term, consistent schedule as prescribed by your doctor.
special_populations: Children: This medicine can be used in children as young as 2 years old for certain conditions. The dose will be based on your child's weight. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It may affect the baby's immune system if used late in pregnancy. Breastfeeding: It is not fully known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Elderly patients: Older adults may have a higher risk of serious infections while taking this medicine. Your doctor will monitor you closely. People with infections or a history of TB: You will need to be tested for tuberculosis and other infections before starting treatment. Do not start this medicine if you have an active infection.
